subject: SLA contingency for LumenHealth deployment — canary auto-failback & pin policy
messages:
From: Kate Evans <kate.evans@lumenhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Production go-live — SLA concerns and request for mitigations

Hi Kimberly,

Quick note from the LumenHealth deployment team: we're planning to route live traffic to the Redwood endpoint next week, but our security and SRE leads want explicit mitigations for potential latency spikes during the first 48 hours. Specifically they asked about automatic fallback behavior for canary/A-B variants, and whether you can guarantee a pin to last-known-good model if response P50 or P95 breaches our SLA windows.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can auto-fail traffic off the canary variant to a stable pin if latency > 1.5s P95 for more than 5 minutes
- If there is an automatic autorevert window and who approves an extended hold
- What telemetry we'll get in real time to make a decision (dashboards/alerts)

Procurement has the contract on standby but wants these controls documented before sign-off.

Thanks,
Kate Evans\Director of Engineering, Integrations\LumenHealth
(attachment: expected_traffic_profile.csv)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Kate Evans <kate.evans@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production go-live — SLA concerns and request for mitigations

Hi Kate — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details below and attached the canary metrics proposal and SLA exception form.

TL;DR:
- Yes: we can configure an automatic failback rule that shifts 100% of canary traffic to the pinned stable model when your P95 latency exceeds 1.5s for a continuous 5-minute window.
- Yes: the pin will remain in effect until a post-mortem and a rolling verification (default 2-hour hold) is completed; we can shorten or extend the hold by mutual agreement documented in the exception form.
- Telemetry: streaming logs, per-route P50/P95/P99, token-level cost, and a ready webhook to fire alerts to your PagerDuty. Dashboard link in attachments.

Details:
- Automatic failback behavior: policy name "LumenHealth-canary-failback-v1". It monitors P95 and error rate. On trigger, traffic is re-pointed atomically to the pinned model and a rollback event is emitted to both parties. We also open an internal incident and tag the customer account for priority triage.
- Pin semantics: pin captures model hash + config (quantization + kernel profile). Pinning prevents autoscaling-driven ephemeral model swaps from being served.
- Safety net: if the pinned model experiences an outage we fall back to the next-approved replica (read: regional fallback) per the contract.

Attachments: canary-metrics-proposal.xlsx (contains thresholds and expected charts), sla_exception_form.pdf (please sign and return).

I'll loop in Rishi for the rapid telemetry hooks and Laura for rollout approvals.

Best,
Kimberly Park\Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference\Redwood Inference
(attachment: canary-metrics-proposal.xlsx; sla_exception_form.pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production go-live — SLA concerns and request for mitigations

Kimberly / team — quick internal coordination. Notes from infra/sre:
- Confirmed we can wire a webhook to Kate's PagerDuty; need their Integration key.
- Recommend adding a secondary trigger: if error rate > 0.5% for 3 minutes AND P95 > 1.2s, then failback immediately. That gives us an early-warning path.
- For the pin hold: 2 hours default is fine, but sales should request a "hot-unlock" flow for one-time emergency unpin (requires VP sign-off).

Aditya — can you draft the language for the exception form to cover the hot-unlock and regional fallback order? Rishi — please prepare a lightweight Dashboard (shared link) and a short test suite we can run during the first hour to validate correctness post-failback.

Laura Bennett\Director, Cloud Reliability (ops)\Redwood Inference
(attachment: trace-snapshot-0518.txt)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Kate Evans <kate.evans@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production go-live — SLA concerns and request for mitigations

Kate — following internal confirmation: we've implemented the two-tier trigger (primary: P95 > 1.5s for 5m; secondary: error rate > 0.5% for 3m AND P95 > 1.2s). On either trigger we will atomically shift traffic to your pinned model and generate an incident with post-mortem cadence.

Next steps for sign-off:
1) Please sign and return the attached SLA exception form (signed pdf) with the chosen hold duration (we put 2h default).
2) Send your PagerDuty integration key to rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai so we can wire alerts.
3) We'll run a 30-minute smoke during the first hour of go-live to validate telemetry and the autorevert is working as expected; we'll share the dashboard link ahead of time.

If procurement needs explicit contract language about the hot-unlock flow (VP sign-off), Aditya will route that to your legal contact.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a short call if you prefer.

Kimberly Park\Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference\kimberly_park@redwood.ai
(attachments referenced: sla_exception_form.pdf)
